text:
viv: Morning team  first day. On M2, using zsh. Ran dotfiles installer but my PATH precedence seems off: `which node` -> /usr/bin/node, asdf shows nodejs 20.6.1 installed. My ~/.zshrc and ~/.zprofile both have lines from the installer. Any rules about what goes where? Also curious where folks put REDWOOD_API_KEY for quick local testing  .env, .local, direnv?
olga: welcome viv :wave: On mac zsh: ~/.zprofile is for login-shell PATH additions, ~/.zshrc is for interactive settings. The installer sometimes writes to both; ensure the PATH prepends asdf shims in ~/.zprofile: ```export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"
eval "$(asdf init zsh)"
``` Then open a new login shell or `source ~/.zprofile`. If you have `/etc/zshenv` or system-wide rc that injects /usr/bin earlier, move the asdf export to the very top.
viv: I had asdf lines in ~/.zshrc below a dotfiles line that sources /etc/zshenv. Moving to ~/.zprofile and restarting terminal fixed node. But my dotfiles installer also adds an `env.local` file to the repo root  is that safe for storing REDWOOD_API_KEY?
marcus: avoid committing keys. We prefer direnv for local dev. Add `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` to a local `.envrc` and `direnv allow`. For quick ephemeral testing you can also use `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` in the shell. 1Password entries are named `redwood-personal-<name>` for personal dev keys; if you need one, ping #support.
devex-bot: (bot) Hi viv! Need a hands-on setup session? Reply "pair" and I'll DM DevEx availability. Onboarding guide: https://handbook.redwood.dev/onboarding/dev-setup.
olga: extra check: run `command -v asdf` and `ls -l ~/.asdf/shims` to confirm shims exist and are executable. If shims are present but `node` still points to /usr/bin, try `hash -r` to clear zsh's command cache.
viv: ran `hash -r` and `which node` updated. Thanks. One more thing: when I try `gem install bundler` it errors with openssl missing during ruby build. Any brew/openssl flags I should export?
marcus: set before installing ruby via asdf: ```export LDFLAGS='-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib'
export CPPFLAGS='-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/include'
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/pkgconfig"
``` Then `asdf install ruby <version>`. Also ensure `brew --prefix` returns `/opt/homebrew` (arm). If it returns `/usr/local` you may be on Rosetta brew and need to reinstall.
viv: brew --prefix was /opt/homebrew so that part's good. Quick weirdness: after enabling direnv, my editor (vscode) didn't pick up the env when running tests in the integrated terminal. Any tricks?
olga: VSCode sometimes launches shells as login/non-login differently. In settings set terminal.integrated.inheritEnv to true, and make sure your VSCode terminal uses the login shell by setting \"terminal.integrated.shellArgs.osx\": [\"-l\"] so ~/.zprofile is sourced. Alternatively add a `.envrc.local` that the project loads and run tests from an external terminal.
viv: that fixed it, thanks. Final oddball: trying to import my GPG signing key gave pinentry errors. Pinentry isn't installed. Quick mac steps?
marcus: `brew install pinentry-mac` then edit `~/.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf` add `pinentry-program /opt/homebrew/bin/pinentry-mac` and `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` in ~/.zprofile. Then `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent && gpgconf --launch gpg-agent`. If you use a hardware key, run `gpg --card-status`.
cloudinfra: quick reminder from infra: never store production secrets in dotfiles. We keep service tokens in 1Password and Vault (for CI). For personal dev API keys use the `redwood-personal-<name>` entry in 1Password; for CI create a ticket in #infra for a scoped token.
devex-bot: (bot) Setup checklist summary posted to your DMs. Reply "pair" to schedule 1:1 help.
viv: all green now  node, ruby, gpg, direnv, editor envs. Huge thanks everyone! :tada:
